Handoff read. Summary of where that work sits, so it doesn't get lost:

- Patch-naming feature (editable title → derived filename → rename prompt) is implemented, 238 tests green, **uncommitted** on `main`.
- One thing never verified: whether the editable title bar commits once or per keystroke. Needs you at a running window.
- Nothing there blocks the MIDI-to-CV work.

Now the patch. What I can already confirm from your repo and the ZOIA manual:

- The catalog has everything needed: `Midi Notes In` (id 20, up to 8 voices, per-voice note/gate/velocity/trigger), `Midi Pitch Bend` (86), `Midi CC In` (21), `Midi Pressure` (35), `Midi Clock In` (82).
- Output side is the fork in the road. The **ZOIA pedal** has exactly **one** CV output — the ring of the control port TRS (`Cport CV Out`, id 55). The **Euroburo** has four dedicated CV outs (ids 87, 99, 100, 101) with selectable 0–10V / 0–5V / ±5V ranges and an A/C transpose option.
- Your repo's `FromScratchExportTests` proves the encoder can build a valid `.bin` from nothing, so I can generate the patch file directly rather than you placing modules by hand.

Three decisions before I build:

questions.question: Which ZOIA is this patch for?

options.label: Euroburo
options.description: 4 dedicated CV outs, 2 CV ins, selectable 0-10V / 0-5V / ±5V per jack plus an A/C transpose option. A real MIDI-to-CV interface is possible here.

options.label: ZOIA pedal
options.description: One CV output only — the ring of the control port TRS, 0-5V. Pitch AND gate cannot both leave the box; I'd have to pick one signal or multiplex, and you'd need a TRS insert cable.

options.label: Both
options.description: Two patch files, one per device, sharing the same MIDI-in side.

questions.question: How many voices should it handle?

options.label: Mono (1 voice)
options.description: One pitch + one gate, plus room on the remaining outs for velocity, mod, or clock. Simplest and most useful for driving one external oscillator.

options.label: Duophonic (2 voices)
options.description: Two pitch/gate pairs — uses all four Euroburo CV outs, leaving nothing for velocity or clock.

options.label: 4-note pitch only
options.description: Four pitch CVs, no gates. Only useful if the receiving gear derives its own envelopes.

questions.question: Beyond pitch and gate, what should reach the CV jacks? Pick in priority order — jack count is the limit.

options.label: Velocity
options.description: Note-on velocity as a CV, for VCA or filter depth.

options.label: Mod wheel (CC1)
options.description: Midi CC In on controller 1. Easy to change the CC number later.

options.label: Pitch bend folded into pitch
options.description: Bend summed onto the note CV rather than sent as its own jack — costs no extra output.

options.label: MIDI clock
options.description: Clock or quarter-note pulse out, for syncing an external sequencer.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a ZOIA (pedal) MIDI-to-CV patch .bin.

Single control-port CV output, with the source of that output selected by
the left stompswitch stepping an 8-step sequencer into an In Switch.

Slot order on the In Switch:
  1 pitch (1V/oct)   2 gate       3 velocity      4 trigger
  5 pitch bend       6 mod wheel  7 aftertouch    8 MIDI clock (quarter)

Pitch scaling: ZOIA note CV is 0.1 per octave (module index: 0 = A0,
1 = A10). Cport CV Out maps 0..1 onto 0-5V, so raw note CV would be
0.5 V/oct. Two CV Mixer channels carrying the same note CV at unity sum
to 2x, giving 1.0 V/oct over a five-octave window starting at A0.
A third mixer channel takes a Value module as a manual octave offset
(0.2 on that knob = +1 octave).
"""
import struct

FILE_SIZE = 32768
HEADER_WORDS = 10          # 8 words + 8 option bytes
NAME_WORDS = 4             # 16-byte module name
FULL = 10000               # 100% connection strength


def w(v):
    return struct.pack('<i', v)


def fixed16(s):
    b = s.encode('ascii')[:16]
    return b + b'\0' * (16 - len(b))


def frac(x):
    return int(round(x * 65535))


class Module:
    def __init__(self, name, type_id, page, color, position, options, params):
        self.name = name
        self.type_id = type_id
        self.page = page
        self.color = color
        self.position = position
        self.options = (list(options) + [0] * 8)[:8]
        self.params = list(params)

    def encode(self):
        size = HEADER_WORDS + len(self.params) + NAME_WORDS
        out = b''.join(w(v) for v in (
            size, self.type_id, 0, self.page, self.color,
            self.position, len(self.params), 0))
        out += bytes(self.options)
        out += b''.join(w(v) for v in self.params)
        out += fixed16('')          # per-module custom name: left blank
        return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- modules
# Index order below IS the module index used by connections.
M_NOTES, M_BEND, M_CC, M_PRESS, M_CLOCK = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4
M_MIXER, M_VALUE = 5, 6
M_SWITCH, M_SEQ, M_STOMP, M_CPORT, M_PIXEL = 7, 8, 9, 10, 11

# Mode-select values: centre of each of the 8 In Switch bands (0..1 / 8).
STEP_VALUES = [frac((k + 0.5) / 8) for k in range(8)]

modules = [
    # 20 Midi Notes In - ch1, 1 voice, newest, not greedy, velocity ON,
    #    low 0, high 127, trigger ON  -> blocks: note, gate, velocity, trigger
    Module('Midi Notes In', 20, 0, 1, 0, [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1], []),
    # 86 Midi Pitch Bend - ch1
    Module('Midi Pitch Bend', 86, 0, 11, 4, [0], []),
    # 21 Midi CC In - ch1, controller 1 (mod wheel), range 0..1
    Module('Midi CC In', 21, 0, 11, 5, [0, 1, 0], []),
    # 35 Midi Pressure - ch1
    Module('Midi Pressure', 35, 0, 11, 6, [0], []),
    # 82 Midi Clock In - quarter out only, beat modifier 1
    Module('Midi Clock In', 82, 0, 5, 7, [0, 0, 0, 0], []),
    # 104 CV Mixer - 3 channels, summing.
    #     params: cv_in 1..3 (cabled, 0) then atten 1..3 (unity = 1.0)
    Module('CV Mixer', 104, 0, 4, 8, [2, 0],
           [0, 0, 0, frac(1.0), frac(1.0), frac(1.0)]),
    # 45 Value - octave offset, 0..1 range. 0.2 = +1 octave. Default 0.
    Module('Value', 45, 0, 4, 16, [0], [0]),
    # 31 In Switch - 8 inputs. params: cv_input 1..8 (cabled) + in_select
    Module('In Switch', 31, 1, 6, 0, [7], [0] * 9),
    # 4 Sequencer - 8 steps, 1 CV track, no restart jack, loop, no key in.
    #    params: step 1..8 then gate_in threshold (0 = advance on any rise)
    Module('Sequencer', 4, 1, 2, 16, [7, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], STEP_VALUES + [0]),
    # 44 Stompswitch - left, momentary, normally zero
    Module('Stompswitch', 44, 1, 3, 32, [0, 0, 0], []),
    # 55 Cport CV Out - input interpreted 0..1, sent as 0-5V on the ring
    Module('Cport CV Out', 55, 1, 8, 33, [0], [0]),
    # 81 Pixel - CV brightness readout of whatever is leaving the jack
    Module('Pixel', 81, 1, 8, 34, [0], [0]),
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------ connections
# (source module, source block position, dest module, dest block position)
connections = [
    # note CV doubled: same source into two summing mixer channels
    (M_NOTES, 0, M_MIXER, 0),
    (M_NOTES, 0, M_MIXER, 1),
    (M_VALUE, 1, M_MIXER, 2),     # manual octave offset
    # the eight selectable sources
    (M_MIXER, 16, M_SWITCH, 0),   # 1 pitch, 1V/oct
    (M_NOTES, 1, M_SWITCH, 1),    # 2 gate
    (M_NOTES, 2, M_SWITCH, 2),    # 3 velocity
    (M_NOTES, 3, M_SWITCH, 3),    # 4 trigger
    (M_BEND, 0, M_SWITCH, 4),     # 5 pitch bend
    (M_CC, 0, M_SWITCH, 5),       # 6 mod wheel (CC1)
    (M_PRESS, 0, M_SWITCH, 6),    # 7 aftertouch
    (M_CLOCK, 0, M_SWITCH, 7),    # 8 MIDI clock, quarter note
    # mode selection
    (M_SEQ, 36, M_SWITCH, 16),    # sequencer track -> in select
    (M_STOMP, 0, M_SEQ, 32),      # left footswitch -> sequencer gate in
    # output
    (M_SWITCH, 17, M_CPORT, 0),
    (M_SWITCH, 17, M_PIXEL, 0),
]

PAGES = ['MIDI IN', 'CV OUT']
PATCH_NAME = 'MIDI to CV'


def build():
    body = fixed16(PATCH_NAME)
    body += w(len(modules))
    for m in modules:
        body += m.encode()

    body += w(len(connections))
    for src, sblk, dst, dblk in connections:
        body += b''.join(w(v) for v in (src, sblk, dst, dblk, FULL))

    body += w(len(PAGES))
    for p in PAGES:
        body += fixed16(p)

    body += w(0)                       # starred params
    for m in modules:
        body += w(m.color)

    out = w(len(body) // 4 + 1) + body  # size word counts itself
    assert len(out) <= FILE_SIZE, len(out)
    return out + b'\0' * (FILE_SIZE - len(out))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    import sys
    data = build()
    path = sys.argv[1]
    with open(path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(data)
    print(f'wrote {path} ({len(data)} bytes, '
          f'{len(modules)} modules, {len(connections)} connections)')

Done. The patch is built, structurally verified against your own decoder, and delivered.

## What it does

One patch, two pages, 12 modules, 15 cables. The single control-port CV jack carries **one of eight sources**, and the **left footswitch** steps through them.

| Slot | Source | Range at the jack |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Pitch, 1V/oct** | 0–5V, A0 at 0V, ceiling A5 |
| 2 | Gate | 0V / 5V, held for note length |
| 3 | Velocity | 0–5V |
| 4 | Trigger | short pulse per note-on |
| 5 | Pitch bend | 0–5V |
| 6 | Mod wheel (CC1) | 0–5V |
| 7 | Aftertouch (channel pressure) | 0–5V |
| 8 | MIDI clock | quarter-note square |

An 8-step Sequencer drives the In Switch select, so the current mode is **visible on the grid** — the lit step tells you which source is on the jack. A Pixel next to the output shows the CV level leaving the box.

## The pitch scaling, since that's the part that matters

ZOIA's note CV runs 0.1 per octave (module index: `0` = A0, `1` = A10). Cport CV Out maps 0–1 onto 0–5V, so raw note CV would give you **0.5 V/oct** — half of what a 1V/oct oscillator wants. The patch fixes that by feeding the same note CV into **two summing CV Mixer channels at unity**, doubling it to 1.0 V/oct.

A third mixer channel takes a **Value** module as a manual octave offset. **0.2 on that knob = +1 octave**, so you can slide the five-octave window to wherever you actually play.

## Before it will work

1. **MIDI in goes to the 1/8" MIDI IN jack**, not the control port — use a Type A dongle. The control port is busy sending CV.
2. **Config Menu → Control Port → `cv`.**
3. **Use a TRS or insert cable.** CV leaves on the **ring**. A TS cable shorts the ring to ground and you get nothing.
4. MIDI channel 1 throughout. Every MIDI module has a channel option if you need to move it.

## What I verified, and what I did not

**Verified** — a temporary test ran against your `PatchDecoder`/`BlockLayout` and passed: 12 modules decode, all 15 cable endpoints land on active blocks of the correct direction, every module's param count matches its active param blocks, no two modules overlap on a page's 40 buttons, and re-encoding reproduces the file byte-for-byte. That test is deleted and your working tree is back to exactly the five modified files plus `PatchNamingTests.swift`.

- **The 1V/oct calibration is derived from the documented note-CV range, not from hardware.** Play A2, then A3; they should sit exactly 1V apart. If the interval is half that, the doubling didn't take and I'll add a fourth mixer channel.
- **Pitch bend is deliberately not summed into the pitch output.** The ZOIA bend CV range isn't documented anywhere I could check, and guessing wrong detunes everything by a constant. It's a selectable source instead. Tell me what bend reads at rest and at full throw and I'll fold it into the pitch channel with the right depth.
- **Sequencer gate-in threshold is set to 0.** If the footswitch double-advances or refuses to advance, turn that knob to about half.

Pushed. `cccfef7..056d32e` on `main` at `github.com:darthzen/zoia-canvas.git`.

- **238 tests in 29 suites passed** before the commit — I ran the suite rather than taking the handoff's word for it.
- Six files: the five modified sources plus `PatchNamingTests.swift`.
- Working tree is clean; `main` tracks `origin/main` with nothing ahead.
- The ZOIA patch files stayed out of it, `dist/` being gitignored.

One thing carried over from the handoff that the commit does not resolve: **the editable title bar has still never been seen running.** If `.navigationTitle(Binding<String>)` calls its setter per keystroke instead of on commit, renaming a saved patch fires the rename alert once per character. The fix is small — buffer the typed name in `@State` and only call `session.rename(to:)` on commit — but it needs you at a window to know whether it's needed:

```bash
open /Users/rashford/DerivedData/ZoiaCanvas-higjgrgqprlsrabhemsburbjpfvz/Build/Products/Debug/ZoiaCanvas.app
```

Click-and-hold the title to check it becomes a field, then rename an already-saved patch and count the alerts.
